{{short description|Swedish mathematician}}
'''Kurt Johansson''' (born 1960) is a [[Sweden|Swedish]] mathematician, specializing in probability theory.

Johansson received his PhD in 1988 from [[Uppsala University]] under the supervision of [[Lennart Carleson]]<ref>{{MathGenealogy|id=19989|title=Kurt Johansson}}</ref> and is a [[professor]] in mathematics at [[KTH Royal Institute of Technology]].<ref>{{cite web|title=Kurt Johansson|website=kth.se|url=https://people.kth.se/~kurtj/}}</ref>

In 2000 Johansson was awarded the [[Rollo Davidson Prize]] in Probability theory. In 2002 he was an invited speaker of the [[International Congress of Mathematicians]] in Beijing<ref>{{cite book|author=Johansson, Kurt|chapter=Toeplitz determinants, random growth and determinant processes|title=Proceedings of the ICM, Beijing 2002|volume=3|pages=53–62|arxiv=math/0304368|year=2003}}</ref> and was awarded the [[Göran Gustafsson Prize]]. In 2006 he was elected a member of the [[Royal Swedish Academy of Sciences]]. In 2012 he was elected a fellow of the [[American Mathematical Society]].
